hydrationEscaping.method: Three fresh-process pairs per runtime/case, alternating candidate order. 5000 warmups, six timed blocks of 20000 calls (5000 dense, 1000 large), explicit GC, Buffer.byteLength consumption. Real case uses unchanged 495-character comparison-fixture hydration JSON. Synthetic state includes sequence=i each call. ASCII x*4000, sparse x*3990 plus < U+2028 U+2029, dense (x < U+2028 U+2029)*1000, large repeats that group 16000 times.

allocation.method: Node only, three fresh-process pairs, 32768-byte sampling interval, collected objects included, 20000 calls (2000 large) after 5000 warmups. Estimated allocated bytes per call, not retained heap.

hydrationEscaping.validation: Node/Bun exact-output checks passed for keys, script delimiters, Unicode, lone surrogates and replacer. Paired UTF-8 totals matched. Production unchanged.
hydrationEscaping.limitations: Shared host. Variable no-match controls limit small timing claims. Bun allocations unmeasured. Dense inputs are synthetic stress cases. No request-throughput or retained-heap claim.
hydrationEscaping.conclusion: Retain guarded singleton regex. Slicing reduced sparse Node time about 9% but did not reduce sampled allocation. Dense slicing allocated about 7% more on Node and took 13% longer on Node, 9% longer on Bun. At 64K characters it took 9% longer on Node and 128% longer on Bun.

ssrSchedulingComparison.method: Local adaptation of measure-ssr-arrivals.mjs. Preserved fixed participant bundle, fresh service, worker and two drivers per case, 30 s target-rate warmup and 60 s measurement. Preliminary captures reverse variant order. Final full-distribution pairs run Node streaming before/after, Bun buffered after/before, then Bun streaming before/after. Percentile ranges span the two driver values, not pooled requests.
ssrSchedulingComparison.bunReproduction: Build the committed Bun adapter. Clone its dist into two local trees. In the control only, transpile render-scheduler.ts from the control commit using workspace TypeScript ES2022/ESNext into render-scheduler.js. Select the before/after adapter through the benchmark worker import. Preserve all other host, renderer and load-driver code. Source maps are not used for measurement. Verify participant and adapter hashes before and after every case. Final full-distribution controls retain the pre-extraction render-policy.js from c8711bfa, while changed adapters use 8a766808 including the shared work window. All final comparisons share the server build from 8a766808.
ssrSchedulingComparison.nodePrototype: Uncommitted diagnostic clone of Node admission.js. Give its checkpoint a streaming capability using Bun createBunRenderPolicy(gate, enqueue).streaming only while the Node gate shouldSchedule() is true. Initial admission and buffered rendering retain their existing behavior. That prototype precedes the committed shared work-window implementation. Final Node comparisons substitute only admission.js from c8711bfa for the before case, retaining the shared server build in both variants.
limitations: These are targeted diagnostics, not a new full comparison baseline.
No fresh reboot. Concurrent user activity and OS scheduling remain uncontrolled.
The two Node cooperative-prototype runs use local generated-code substitutions. Final Node comparisons use committed admission source compiled with the same ES2022/ESNext TypeScript settings.
The first Node comparison ran while unrelated Bun source changes were committed. Node and participant outputs were frozen and verified.
The historical low tail latencies remain unreproduced.
ssrSchedulingComparison.distributionMethod: Response timing runs from driver request issue through complete response receipt. Means are weighted by request count across the two drivers. Each percentile is a range of driver values, never an average or pooled percentile. P75 exists only in the three final verify runs. Warmup is retained separately.

outcome.bunStreaming: Strong improvement across all captured percentiles and throughput. Final control missed 17,865 of 480,000 arrivals, versus 2 with the fix.
outcome.bunBuffered: Small tail tradeoff accepted alongside the streaming benefit. Final mean rises about 0.04 ms and P99 about 2.3 ms at unchanged offered throughput.
outcome.nodeStreaming: Mean, P95 and P99 improve. Median and P75 remain essentially unchanged. Prototype benefits repeated in reversed order and both committed-code comparisons.
outcome.historicalGap: These fixes improve the currently reproducible workload. They do not establish why historical low tails stopped reproducing with the earlier document and unchanged Node adapter.
outcome.responseIdentity: All before/after final response identities match, with zero response errors during warmup and measurement.

nodeStreamingFetchComparison.conclusion: The streaming work-window change reproduces an 11–15% ordinary-fetching throughput loss in reversed matched pairs. Restoring batching while retaining window bookkeeping recovers most of the loss. Both gate policies predominantly select scheduling, so the regression is in the selected checkpoint policy rather than failure to enable admission.
nodeStreamingFetchComparison.recommendation: Keep fully batched streaming as an alternative in the existing adaptive controller. Compare it with budgeted streaming rather than replacing that candidate globally.
limitations: This isolates a scheduling-policy cause, not individual V8 or networking CPU functions.

geography.observedWork: Each edit still invalidates 34 sources, analyzes 17 callable sources and rebuilds the program once. The optimized ordinary-module request performs no component source analyses or placement link walks. Component requests compute the deferred fixed point from fresh facts.

completeEditPass.method: Each of three fresh JSON-protocol sessions per compiler synchronizes and compiles all 34 prepared sources outside the timer.
